claim: Henderson et al.'s 'Deep Reinforcement Learning that Matters' was published at AAAI 2018, not 2017, despite Semantic Scholar and many citing papers listing it as 2017.
stance_target: user-flagged citation trap: 'Henderson is AAAI 2018 (S2 says 2017)'
scope_conditions: Publication metadata printed directly on the paper's first page
quoted_support: "Copyright c 2018, Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence (www.aaai.org). All rights reserved."

claim: The '2017' date commonly attached to Henderson et al. traces to the arXiv preprint posting date (Sept 2017), which is also the version Melis et al. (2017/2018) cite in their own reference list.
stance_target: explaining mechanism behind the citation trap
scope_conditions: Cross-reference between Melis et al.'s bibliography and Henderson et al.'s arXiv submission history
quoted_support: Melis et al. reference list: "Peter Henderson, Riashat Islam, Philip Bachman, Joelle Pineau, Doina Precup, and David Meger. Deep reinforcement learning that matters. arXiv preprint arXiv:1709.06560, 2017."

claim: Henderson et al. demonstrate that deep RL policy-gradient benchmark comparisons can flip based on codebase, network architecture, activation function, and random seed count alone, independent of the underlying algorithm.
scope_conditions: Continuous control policy-gradient methods (TRPO, PPO, DDPG, ACKTR) on standard MuJoCo benchmarks
quoted_support: "In (Islam et al. 2017), it is shown that policy network architecture can significantly impact results in both TRPO and DDPG."
